brief: Given array b, pick K elements to maximize total happiness. Follow-ups: rearrange two arrays to minimize or maximize the sum of a[i]*b[i].
key_idea: Taking the K largest values is optimal. For products, pairing sorted orders (opposite for min, same for max) is optimal by an exchange argument.
solution: 1. Sort b ascending and add the last K elements to the sum.
2. Min sum of products: sort a ascending, sort b descending, pair index by index.
3. Max sum of products: sort both ascending, pair index by index.
4. Exchange argument: swapping a pair that is out of order changes the sum by (a4-a2)*(b2-b4) >= 0, so the sorted pairing is never worse.
complexity: O(N log N) time, O(1) extra space
dry_run: a=[1,3,-5], b=[-2,4,1]: min pairing gives -25, max pairing gives 23 (both checked by the C++).
leetcode_match: none verified; closest greedy-by-sort pattern is LC 1005 (see 18q)
